title: The scanner's equations, solved by other code

rows.quantity: RF-spoiled steady state of spgr and afi (hard pulses, no diffusion)
rows.reference: independent_bloch.spoiled_gre: 2,048 isochromats over one spoiler cycle, 3 x 3 rotations, time stepping from equilibrium

rows.quantity: rotation made by the windowed-sinc pulse at every position through the slice (Cayley-Klein parameters), 10 to 180 degrees, time-bandwidth 2 / 4 / 8
rows.reference: independent_bloch.shaped_pulse acting on the three unit vectors, sample by sample

rows.quantity: RF-spoiled gradient echo integrated over the slice (time-bandwidth 2 / 4 / 8)
rows.reference: independent_bloch.slice_gre: isochromats over (position through the slice) x (96 spoiler phases), the 128-sample pulse stepped under its slice gradient for each of them in every repetition
rows.note: With T1 / T2 relaxation during a 2 ms pulse, which the scanner's model leaves out, the same integrator gives a signal 0.05 % away (20 degrees, TR 20 ms, T1 400 ms, T2 50 ms): a declared difference, not a tolerance.

rows.quantity: spin echo and inversion recovery integrated over the slice: shaped 90 and 180 degree pulses, crushers, B1 80 to 115 %
rows.reference: independent_bloch.slice_se: isochromats over (position) x (32 crusher phases), both pulses stepped under their gradients; the longitudinal magnetisation is averaged over the crusher phases after every echo, as the scanner's model states
rows.note: A refocusing pulse that is not 180 degrees everywhere stores a grating of longitudinal magnetisation, which identical crushers recall in the next repetition (a stimulated echo). The scanner's model leaves it out. With the grating kept, the same integrator gives -2 to +39 % of the served signal in these 5 cases (TR 300 to 2000 ms, T1 500 to 1200 ms): a declared difference, not a tolerance.

rows.quantity: balanced SSFP against off-resonance (hard pulses, 41 precession angles per TR; RF phase advance 180, 90 and 300 degrees per TR)
rows.reference: independent_bloch.bssfp: time stepping to the steady state, the phase turning the axis of every pulse

rows.quantity: inversion time that nulls an inversion-recovery spin echo at finite TR and inversion efficiency 0.85 to 1
rows.reference: independent_bloch.ir_null: the longitudinal chain stepped through 40 repetitions, bisection

rows.quantity: slice gradient of the three selective pulses, in nominal bandwidths across the prescribed thickness (1.197 / 0.994 / 1.000)
rows.reference: independent_bloch.slice_calibration: the width at half maximum of the transverse magnetisation that a 0.0001 degree pulse leaves on single isochromats, by bisection

rows.quantity: RF-spoiled steady state with a saturation pulse (Mz x q, 6.5 to 8 ms before every excitation; 50 to 100 % saturated)
rows.reference: independent_bloch.spoiled_gre with the saturation as a step of the time stepping: 1,024 isochromats
rows.note: The saturation acts on the longitudinal magnetisation only, in the scanner and in the integrator: what a real pulse does to the transverse magnetisation of earlier repetitions is left out of both (limits.md, block 9a).

not_run: per-pulse transient of the first 300 pulses: the scanner serves the periodic state only
